title: I Told the Truth in the AITA About the Birthday Restaurant

parts.text: I refused to split the bill evenly after she ordered the lobster I could not afford. I am twenty-three, office starter, birthday dinner for my friend Noor, who is lovely and has champagne taste on a group tab. I ate pasta, $18. She ate lobster, $64, plus shots I declined. The table wanted even split because vibes. The waiter, Luis, hovered with the book. I asked for separate. Someone called me cheap. I am cheap. I also pay rent. Noor looked pained, then said she would cover her lobster, which is why she is still my friend. The others learned math in public. The pasta was fine. The bread basket smelled like garlic and social death. I still went to karaoke after because I am not a monk. I sang badly. I paid for my soda. AITA: maybe a little, for not pre-gaming the rule. Also NTA, for not funding lobster as friendship. I now say separate checks when we sit down, like a spell. Friend said, "Don't make it weird, just split" I said, "I can pay for pasta. Not lobster" Luis muttered that's easier anyway. Waiters know. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened.

social.video_title: I asked for a separate check after the lobster
social.description: Garlic bread, $18 pasta, $64 lobster, karaoke soda. Vibes are not a tax. Would you have split anyway?
